categories.title: Ripper
categories.description: Deep-fried hot dogs, cooked until their casing “rips”. Originated in Passaic & Bergen counties.

categories.title: “Dirty Water” Dog
categories.description: Boiled hot dogs served from pushcarts and concession stands, often with classic toppings like relish and sauerkraut.

categories.title: Chili Dog
categories.description: Many hot dogs have chili alone as the focal topping. In New Jersey, chili rarely has beans and may or may not include meat.

categories.title: Plainfield Texas Weiner
categories.description: Plainfield-style Texas Weiners, originating near Plainfield, NJ, include mustard, onions, and a dry, spicy, and dark chili.

categories.title: Passaic Texas Weiner
categories.description: Passaic-style Texas Weiners, originating in Paterson, NJ, include mustard, onions, and a sweet chili sauce.

categories.title: Hot Onions
categories.description: Hot onions are a very spicy, rich topping often served by trucks and carts in and around Branch Brook Park in Newark, NJ. The hot onions are a twist on the classic onion sauce found nationwide.

categories.title: Easton
categories.description: Easton-style dogs include a pickle slice as a topping along with mustard and onions. They can be found on both sides of the Delaware River near Warren County, NJ.

categories.title: Italian
categories.description: Italian Hot Dogs include potatoes, peppers, and onions, and are usually served either in a “pizza roll” in North Jersey, or on a hoagie roll in the Trenton substyle.

categories.title: Jumbo
categories.description: Jumbo franks - usually griddled - are served down the Shore at beachside huts and local restaurants.

categories.title: Wurst
categories.description: New Jersey’s diverse ethnic population ensures that German and Central European style wursts & sausages can be enjoyed all over the state.

categories.title: Farm
categories.description: The Garden State boasts a variety of farms and agricultural businesses which produce high-quality franks made with local beef, pork, and other farm products.

categories.title: Deli
categories.description: Hot dogs served at delicatessens in the state are often Kosher or Kosher-style, and use all-beef franks from quality producers.

categories.title: Distributed
categories.description: “Distributed” hot dogs are defined by how they are sold - en masse at chain restaurants, ballgames, and retail stores.

categories.title: Haute
categories.description: Haute dogs are defined by unique meats, crazy toppings, alternative cooking styles, and unusual formats.
